claims.statement: Afamelanotide (SCENESSE) is FDA-approved as a subcutaneous implant to increase pain-free light exposure in adult patients with a history of phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP); it is not approved for tanning, cosmetic pigmentation, or any indication in patients without a diagnosis of EPP.

context.population: adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) and a history of phototoxic reactions
context.useCase: reduction of phototoxic sun-exposure reactions in EPP
context.doseText: One 16 mg implant administered subcutaneously every 2 months, inserted 3-4 cm above the anterior supra-iliac crest by a trained healthcare professional (label text; not a use recommendation).

claims.statement: In two pivotal multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in EPP patients (US trial, n=94 over 6 months; EU trial, n=74 over 9 months), afamelanotide implants significantly increased pain-free sun exposure time versus placebo (US: median 69.4 vs 40.8 hours, p=0.04; EU: median 6.0 vs 0.8 hours, p=0.005) and the EU trial also showed fewer phototoxic reactions with afamelanotide (77 vs 146, p=0.04).

context.population: adults with confirmed erythropoietic protoporphyria (EU trial n=74: 38 afamelanotide/36 placebo; US trial n=94: 48 afamelanotide/45 placebo)
context.useCase: reduction of phototoxic reactions / increase in pain-free sunlight exposure in EPP
context.doseText: 16 mg implant every 60 days for the duration of the respective 6-month (US) or 9-month (EU) trial period (trial protocol; not a use recommendation).

extractedEvidence.quote: Median, 69.4 hours, vs. 40.8 hours in the placebo group; P=0.04
Median, 6.0 hours vs. 0.8 hours; P=0.005

In the U.S. study, the duration of pain-free time after 6 months was longer in the afamelanotide group (median, 69.4 hours, vs. 40.8 hours in the placebo group; P = 0.04). In the European Union study, the duration of pain-free time after 9 months was also longer in the afamelanotide group than in the placebo group (median, 6.0 hours vs. 0.8 hours; P = 0.005), and the number of phototoxic reactions was lower in the afamelanotide group (77 vs. 146, P = 0.04).

claims.statement: In the pivotal EU/US placebo-controlled trials, adverse events with afamelanotide were mostly mild (most commonly headache, nausea, and nasopharyngitis); serious adverse events occurred at low rates and were judged unrelated to study drug. Postmarketing surveillance per FDA labeling has additionally identified serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, and the label recommends twice-yearly full-body skin examinations because afamelanotide can darken pre-existing nevi and freckles.

context.population: EPP patients in pivotal RCTs and postmarketing users of SCENESSE

extractedEvidence.quote: Adverse events were mostly mild; serious adverse events were not thought to be related to the study drug.
Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported
may induce darkening of pre-existing nevi and ephelides
Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with postmarket use of SCENESSE. Warn patients of the risk of hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis.

SCENESSE may lead to generalized increased skin pigmentation and darkening of pre-existing nevi and ephelides because of its pharmacologic effect. A full body skin examination (twice yearly) is recommended to monitor pre-existing and new skin pigmentary lesions.

claims.statement: Afamelanotide is frequently marketed and sold online as 'Melanotan I' or a cosmetic tanning injectable for skin darkening in people without EPP; this gray-market use is distinct from and not supported by the FDA-approved SCENESSE product, which requires physician administration, refrigerated implant supply, and REMS-adjacent monitoring, and FDA has taken enforcement action against unapproved injectable tanning products (Melanotan II) for being unapproved new drugs sold with unsubstantiated health claims. No RCT evidence in this packet's source set evaluated afamelanotide/Melanotan I for cosmetic tanning outcomes or safety in the self-injected, unsupervised gray-market context.
